summary: The Commonwealth Master's Scholarships pay for one year of full-time taught master's study at an approved UK university. They are run by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK with money from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. They are for people from 43 eligible low and middle income Commonwealth countries who could not afford UK study without help. The award gives tuition, a monthly stipend, return airfare, a study travel grant and extra allowances for some scholars. Candidates cannot apply to the Commission directly: they apply through a nominating organisation and through the CSC online application portal.
eligibility_notes:
Country and status: the applicant must be a citizen of an eligible Commonwealth country, or have been granted refugee status by one, or be a British Protected Person. The applicant must also live permanently in an eligible country. The 43 eligible countries are Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Saint Helena, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia. Applications from Small Island Developing States are especially welcome.

Degree: by September 2027 the applicant must hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a master's). Disabled applicants without a 2:1 may be considered for a contextualised nomination through the Commonwealth Disabled People's Forum. Applicants who have not finished their first degree can still apply if it will be finished by the start year. The CSC prefers applicants who have completed their first degree and would not normally fund a second master's; a second master's must be justified.

Other conditions: the applicant must be unable to afford UK study without the scholarship, must be free to start by the beginning of the 2027 academic year, and must provide all documents in the required format. There is no age limit and no work experience requirement. The CSC does not require an IELTS or other English test, but universities may ask for one.

Not eligible: anyone who has already studied at master's level at a UK institution, or already held a Commonwealth Scholarship at master's level; nationals of countries not on the list; current or former UK government employees or their relatives (former employees may apply three years after leaving); staff of the Association of Commonwealth Universities or the British Council; current or former Commonwealth Scholarship Commissioners or their relatives; and anyone barred for a bribery conviction under UK law (up to five years). Applications that do not clearly name the qualification sought may be ruled ineligible.

Exclusions of study: MBA degrees are not funded. The FAQ also says research master's degrees are not funded. The CSC gives no new direct support to the overseas fossil fuel energy sector.
age_experience_notes: No age limit. Work experience is not required; applicants set out their employment history and how it supports the planned study.
funding_summary: The award pays the full approved tuition fee for one year of full-time study, a monthly stipend (GBP 1,712, or GBP 2,000 at London-area universities), an approved return airfare, a study travel grant, and visa costs. Scholars who are widowed, divorced or single parents can receive a child allowance. A needs assessment is offered to disabled scholars. The award covers one degree only, and other awards covering the same costs cannot be held at the same time.
programmes_note: One-year, full-time taught master's programmes only, under the six CSC development themes: science and technology for development; improving population health, health systems and capacity; promoting innovation and entrepreneurship; strengthening peace, security and governance; strengthening resilience and response to crises; and access, inclusion and opportunity. The FAQ says study must also relate to one of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. MBAs, research master's degrees and part-time study are not funded. Applicants name three preferred universities and courses in order.
institutions_note: Scholars are placed only at UK universities that have signed an agreement with the CSC under which the university pays 20% of the overseas tuition fee and any fee above the CSC cap. The universities on the CSC list are: Aberystwyth University, Anglia Ruskin University, Aston University, Bangor University, Bath Spa University, Bournemouth University, Brunel University London, Cardiff University, Cardiff Metropolitan University, City St George's University of London, Cranfield University, Durham University, Edge Hill University, Edinburgh Napier University, Glasgow Caledonian University, Goldsmiths University of London, Harper Adams University, Imperial College London, Keele University, King's College London, Kingston University, Lancaster University, Leeds Beckett University, Liverpool Hope University, Liverpool John Moores University, Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, London School of Economics and Political Science, London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Loughborough University, Manchester Metropolitan University, Newcastle University, Northumbria University, Queen Margaret University, Queen Mary University of London, Queen's University Belfast, Robert Gordon University, Royal Holloway University of London, Royal Veterinary College, Sheffield Hallam University, SOAS University of London, Staffordshire University, Swansea University, Teesside University, The Glasgow School of Art, Ulster University, University College London, and the Universities of Aberdeen, Bath, Birmingham, Bradford, Brighton, Bristol, Cambridge, Chester, East Anglia, Edinburgh, Essex, Exeter, Glasgow, Greenwich, Hertfordshire, Huddersfield, Hull, Kent, Leeds, Leicester, Liverpool, Manchester, Northampton, Nottingham, Oxford, Plymouth, Portsmouth, Reading, Salford, Sheffield, Southampton, St Andrews, Stirling, Strathclyde, Surrey, Sussex, the West of England, the West of Scotland, Warwick, Westminster, Worcester and York, plus York St John University. Applicants list three universities and courses in order of preference; the CSC makes the final placement and may overrule the preference. The CSC will not change a provisionally selected candidate's university or course except in exceptional circumstances.

summary.detail: One-year, full-time taught master's at an approved UK university that has an agreement with the CSC. Study is under the six CSC development themes. MBA, research master's and part-time study are not funded. The award covers one degree only, and no other course may be taken at the same time. Language of study is not stated by the CSC; it does not require an English test but universities may.

benefits.limit_text: Full approved tuition fees, agreed between the CSC and the university
benefits.conditions: The scholar pays no part of the tuition fee. The university pays 20% of the overseas fee and any amount above the CSC fee cap.

benefits.limit_text: GBP 1,712 per month; GBP 2,000 per month at London-area universities
benefits.conditions: Current rates. The stipend is paid for the one-year course.

benefits.limit_text: Approved return airfare between the home country and the UK
benefits.conditions: Fares for dependants and journeys made before the award is confirmed are not covered. A scholar who does not leave the UK within one month of the end of the scholarship or programme (whichever is earlier) may lose the airfare and excess baggage entitlements.

benefits.limit_text: Study travel grant for study-related travel within the UK or overseas (no amount stated)
benefits.conditions: Overseas travel during the award needs the CSC's prior approval.
The FAQ states that the award covers visa costs for study in the UK; the page for the Master's Scholarships does not give details. Student visa rules are set by the UK immigration authority.

benefits.limit_text: Child allowance GBP 622 per month for the first child; GBP 154 per month for each of the second and third child under 16
benefits.conditions: Only for scholars who are widowed, divorced or single parents with children living with them at the same address in the UK. Family allowances are a partial contribution, and scholars must top them up to support accompanying family.

benefits.limit_text: Individual needs assessment and extra support for disabled scholars
benefits.conditions: The CSC offers a full needs assessment and eligibility review for additional support.

benefits.limit_text: Overlapping awards, MBA fees and part-time study are not funded
benefits.conditions: Other awards covering the same costs cannot be held at the same time as the scholarship.

requirements.text: Valid passport or national ID card showing photo, date of birth and citizenship. Refugees give equivalent proof of status.

Full transcripts of all higher education qualifications, including to-date transcripts for courses still in progress. Certified translations are needed if they are not in English. A missing transcript or page makes the application ineligible; if to-date transcripts cannot be obtained, an explanation is required. Transcripts are uploaded in the portal.

At least two references, each signed, in PDF, on institutional letterhead or sent from an email that shows the sender's details. Referees write in their own words. The applicant names three referees, one a current employer if applicable. References are uploaded through the portal by the deadline; the CSC accepts no other route.

Four-part development impact statement: how the scholarship relates to development issues and the chosen CSC theme; how the new skills will be used; expected outcomes, timeframe and beneficiaries; and how the impact could be measured.
Personal statement on background and motivation to make an impact at home, including any barriers overcome, and a summary of voluntary activities and leadership.
Detailed plan of study and the objectives of the award and how the course will meet them; three preferred universities and courses in order, with reasons.

Qualification, employment and achievement details on the form: all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications, up to 10 publications and prizes, employment history and how it supports the study, and career plans for the five years after the scholarship and the long term.

Application to a nominating organisation (a national nominating agency or a selected NGO or charity) in addition to the application in the CSC online portal. The nominator may set its own extra criteria and deadlines.
Health and Disability Form, completed after provisional selection and before the award is confirmed.

application_steps.title: Apply to a nominating organisation
application_steps.detail: Candidates cannot apply to the CSC directly. They apply to a nominator: either a national nominating agency (the main route) or a selected NGO or charity. Each nominator sets its own process, deadlines and extra criteria, and nomination does not guarantee selection.

application_steps.title: Submit the application in the CSC online portal
application_steps.detail: The application goes through the CSC online portal and no fee is charged. Draft the answers offline and use the save function, because refreshing the browser loses unsaved data. Two-step login is needed each time. Applications cannot be edited after submission, and late applications are not accepted. References must be uploaded in the portal by the deadline.

application_steps.title: Nominators send their nominations to the CSC
application_steps.detail: Nominators set their own closing dates and must send their nominations to the CSC by December 2026. The CSC then assesses the applications against its three criteria: candidate merit, quality of study plan, and development impact.

application_steps.title: Assessment on merit, study plan and development impact
application_steps.detail: Merit uses exam results, transcripts and referee reports, plus prizes, publications and professional experience. The study plan is judged on what the candidate wants to learn and how well the course and university were researched; an existing offer of admission counts as a secondary sign. Development impact looks at the need, expected outcomes, beneficiaries and the plan to use new skills, with leadership, volunteering and national priorities as secondary points.

application_steps.title: Provisional selection, due diligence and placement
application_steps.detail: Provisional selection depends on agreeing admission terms with a university; the CSC makes the final placement and may overrule the candidate's preference, considering suitability and value for money. Candidates must agree to due diligence checks or the process ends. Outcomes are expected by July 2027; an offer can be withdrawn if the candidate does not reply in time.

application_steps.title: Receive the Notification and Confirmation of Award
application_steps.detail: After the admission terms are agreed the CSC sends the Notification of Award. The scholar then completes the Health and Disability Form, and the CSC issues the Confirmation of Award once all conditions are met. The scholar must start on the date in the Notification and meet the UK visa rules.

application_steps.title: Study in the UK and return home
application_steps.detail: Scholars must live in the UK, need CSC approval for overseas travel and for paid work, and must follow the CSC Code of Conduct and policies. They sign an undertaking to return home before the student visa ends and may not switch to a graduate or other visa to stay. Awards can be ended for poor conduct, progress or attendance. Scholars must leave the UK within one month of the end of the scholarship or programme, whichever is earlier.
